intro.heading: How Invisalign works
paragraphs: Invisalign straightens teeth with a series of clear, BPA-free plastic aligners made for your mouth. Each set moves your teeth a small step, and you switch to a new set every one to two weeks. You wear them 20 to 22 hours a day and remove them to eat, brush and floss, so there are no food restrictions and no change to your hygiene routine.

At Valencia Dentistry, planning starts with the iTero digital scanner rather than impression trays. The scan builds an interactive map of your smile and lets you preview where your teeth are headed. Dr. Moezzi, an Invisalign-certified provider, designs the plan and sees you at every check-in. Most patients in Santa Clarita finish within 6 to 18 months.

whoItsFor.heading: Who it's for
whoItsFor.intro: Invisalign suits many teens and adults who want straighter teeth without braces, including those with:
items: Teeth that have shifted after past orthodontic work
A preference for a discreet, low-maintenance option

benefits.heading: Invisalign compared with metal braces
benefits.intro: The comparison below reflects typical differences; your case may vary.

items.title: Nearly invisible
items.text: Clear aligners are hard to notice. Metal brackets and wires are not.

items.title: More comfortable
items.text: Smooth plastic sits gently against lips and cheeks, with no brackets to rub.

items.title: Removable
items.text: Take them out to eat, brush and floss. Braces are fixed and need special cleaning tools.

items.title: No diet restrictions
items.text: Eat what you normally eat. Braces rule out sticky, chewy and hard foods.

items.title: Fewer office visits
items.text: Quick check-ins every 6 to 8 weeks instead of frequent adjustment appointments.

items.title: Shorter average treatment
items.text: Typically 6 to 18 months, compared with 18 to 24 months for braces.

process.heading: Your Invisalign plan, step by step
process.intro: Five steps from scan to finished smile.

steps.title: Digital scan
steps.text: A quick, mess-free iTero scan creates a high-resolution, interactive map of your teeth. No impression trays.

steps.title: Custom aligners
steps.text: Dr. Moezzi designs your treatment plan, and a set of BPA-free aligners is made specifically for your mouth.

steps.title: Daily wear
steps.text: Wear your aligners 20 to 22 hours a day, removing them only to eat, brush and floss. Your diet and hygiene routine stay the same.

steps.title: Progress check-ins
steps.text: Regular visits every 6 to 8 weeks confirm your teeth are tracking. You move to a new set of aligners every 1 to 2 weeks.

steps.title: Finished smile
steps.text: Most patients complete treatment in 6 to 18 months, depending on how much correction is needed.

technology.heading: iTero digital planning
technology.intro: The scanner does more than replace impressions.

items.title: iTero digital scanner
items.text: Captures your teeth in minutes with no trays or putty, for precise, comfortable impressions.

items.title: Smile preview
items.text: The scan models your projected result so you can see where your teeth are headed before you begin.

items.title: Digital X-rays
items.text: Confirm roots, bone and jaw are healthy before orthodontic movement begins.

cost.heading: Cost and financing
cost.text: Invisalign in Santa Clarita typically ranges from $3,500 to $8,000, depending on how complex your case is and how long treatment takes. Many dental plans with orthodontic benefits cover part of the cost, and our front desk will check your coverage before you commit. After your consultation and scan, you receive a written estimate with the full fee and a monthly financing option, so there are no surprises later. If you are new to the practice, the $59 new patient special covers the exam and X-rays that come first.

faqs.a: Invisalign typically costs between $3,500 and $8,000, depending on case complexity, treatment length and insurance coverage. At your consultation we give you a personalized written estimate and walk you through payment and financing options, so you know the full cost before you start.

faqs.q: How long does Invisalign treatment take?
faqs.a: Most patients finish within 6 to 18 months. Simple spacing or mild crowding sits at the shorter end; bite corrections take longer. Wearing your aligners the full 20 to 22 hours a day is the single biggest factor in staying on schedule.

Invisalign is generally more comfortable than traditional braces. When you move to a new set of aligners you may feel mild pressure or tightness for a day or two, which is the aligners doing their work. It usually eases quickly. There are no wires or brackets to irritate your cheeks.

faqs.q: Can I eat with my aligners in?
faqs.a: No. Remove your aligners before eating or drinking anything other than water. Food and colored drinks can stain or warp the plastic and trap sugar against your teeth. Rinse, brush if you can, and put the aligners back in so you keep up your daily wear time.

faqs.q: How do I clean my Invisalign trays?
faqs.a: Brush your aligners daily with a soft toothbrush and clear, gentle soap, then rinse in lukewarm water. Avoid hot water, which can warp the plastic, and avoid colored or abrasive toothpaste. Invisalign cleaning crystals are another option if you prefer a soak.

faqs.q: How often do I need to visit the office during treatment?
faqs.a: Plan on a visit every 6 to 8 weeks. Dr. Moezzi checks that your teeth are tracking to the plan and hands you your next sets of aligners. These appointments are short, and because you see the same dentist each time, nothing gets lost between visits.

Many dental insurance plans with orthodontic benefits cover part of the cost of Invisalign. Coverage varies by plan and sometimes by age. Our front desk team can check your benefits before your consultation and explain exactly what your plan contributes and what remains.

faqs.q: What's the difference between Invisalign and traditional braces?
faqs.a: Invisalign uses clear, removable aligners; braces use metal brackets and wires fixed to the teeth. Both are effective. Invisalign is more discreet, lets you eat and clean normally and usually needs fewer visits. Braces can be the better choice for some complex cases, which Dr. Moezzi will tell you at your consultation.
